requirement: An annotation or outline item may carry an action to perform on activation; this is a trigger-site statement, not an obligation to implement every action subtype.
errata: No applicable EC3 correction found in doc/errata-read.md or the effective EC3 text.
evidence: Link annotations read /A through action::read and their links expose GoTo destinations; outline activation reads /A and scans the flattened chain for GoTo; annotation event routes perform actions through ViewState::perform_all. Catalog /OpenAction is split by shape: Destination::open_action applies a GoTo destination, while script_sites::open_action handles JavaScript chains. Generic catalog actions are not passed through the ordinary action perform route, and the viewer opening path explicitly notes that action OpenAction is not performed. Screen annotations and FDF fields listed in the paragraph are outside this tree's supported families. Existing tests exercise annotation triggers and OpenAction destinations/scripts, but do not prove generic non-GoTo OpenAction execution; this is a scope boundary for §12.6.1's broad framing, not evidence that every action type is required here. Tests read and inspected; not run in this audit.
test_result: Not run in this audit.

requirement: Next may contain one action dictionary or an array; array members are performed in array order, and each member's own Next subtree is performed before proceeding to its next sibling.
errata: No applicable EC3 correction found.
evidence: push() appends the current recognized action, then walks a dictionary or array. For array elements the loop recursively calls push before the next sibling, producing depth-first order. The cited test's root array has URI then JavaScript; the URI's Next is Launch. Its exact expected Hide, URI, Launch, JavaScript distinguishes depth-first order from breadth-first and checks the root precedes children. Fixture is a parser-local synthetic document without a page tree; this is adequate for action::read's direct dictionary walk but not a complete PDF conformance witness. The separate test draft checks occurrence preservation when an indirect reference appears twice in one array, which the current global visited-set suppresses. Parent: Table196 requires array actions in order; no text collapses two non-cyclic occurrences into one. This is an inferred consequence of that ordered sequence, not an explicit duplicate-reference sentence. Exact reader output drops the second LastPage occurrence.
test_command: link-actions-reviewed-target.log
test_result: FAIL after distinct-member order positive control PASS

requirement: Interactive processors are recommended to handle anomalous action graphs reasonably; in particular, a self-referential action ought not execute more than once. This is recommendation-level cycle robustness, not a producer permission to create cycles.
errata: No applicable EC3 correction found.
evidence: The global BTreeSet of visited indirect object IDs bounds cycles, and the cited two-node Hide/Launch cycle asserts exactly two outputs. This demonstrates a closing-cycle guard and termination. The current mechanism also drops a later non-cyclic occurrence of a previously visited action object in a sibling array; the normative text specifically recommends at-most-once for self-reference, while separately requiring ordered array actions. The draft regression isolates that tension. The note does not mandate this particular global deduplication policy. Tests read and inspected; not run here.
test_result: Not run in this audit.

requirement: It is recommended that an action not modify its own action dictionary or another dictionary in its action tree; effects of such mutation on later sequence execution are undefined.

evidence: Merge write path inventory: write.rs::finish emits StructTreeRoot /K from every retained top element. If wrapper.rs selected at least two top-level PDF 2.0 Documents, finish substitutes one wrapper at the first selected top and suppresses the other selected top-level slots; wrapper_element creates the new StructTreeRoot -> Document edge, and its /K creates new Document -> source-Document edges. write.rs::element rebuilds each kept source element /K from hierarchy.rs::keep child results and sets each /P to the recorded surviving parent (or output root/wrapper). Those are source edges reconstructed after pruning; they retain their pair but pruning can change occurrence counts. Source top edges not wrapped remain top-level output edges. Content items (integer, MCR, OBJR) are not structure-element pairs in Table L.2. The merge does not implement a general Table L.2 pair/count validator. P/Table and WP/Figure are not synthesized by the merge; if present in the source tree they flow through the same retained /K edge path. Under EC3 #83 and #440 those respective pairs are permitted at 0..n in both directions. Existing tests cover the newly added root/wrapper/document edges only. ADR 1474 explicitly says one source's pre-existing Annex L violation is carried as written; that distinguishes source preservation from a reader rejection policy, but it does not prove the entire writer table claim. The shared Carry path is also used by split.rs::plan_structure with one source, so split adds no cross-source wrapper and reconstructs only surviving source edges. archive/tagged.rs creates Part -> P relationships for an appended page, but those elements state no /NS and therefore use the PDF 1.7 default namespace under §14.8.6.1, outside Annex L. requirement: Parse the fragment as a sequence of parameters; separate parameters with the named AMPERSAND character, separate multiple arguments with COMMA, and process/execute parameters from left to right. errata: None affecting §O.2 found.
evidence: Fragment::parse splits on '&', then on ',' before percent-decoding each argument; it retains successful parameters in input order. Open::apply_fragment iterates that vector in order. The parser test asserts both orders are retained; the viewer test uses page=5&comment=... versus comment=...&page=5 and checks focus only in the former case, making the order behavior observable. The parser chooses '=' as the name/argument join although §O.2 does not specify it, as documented in the implementation; this remains a documented syntax choice rather than a normative Annex O rule. It follows AMPERSAND by the character name despite the erroneous 28h code, cross-checked against Table D.2.
test_result: The parser order and comment-order end-to-end tests passed in model-tests-with-worker.log and interaction-tests.log, respectively.

evidence: The clause says to escape bytes in a relative file specification when the filesystem is URL-based, while §7.11.5 says /FS /URL /F is already an RFC 3986 URL with its own character-encoding requirements. A draft using non-ASCII raw bytes in /FS /URL /F is nonconforming input and does not prove a defect. No route was found that opens the source PDF through a URL-based filesystem and then resolves an ordinary relative file specification. The current GoToE path handles /FS /URL, emits the URI as NeedsFile, and the host routes TargetRoot through read_import (under_remote_documents=false), which treats an absolute URL as a local path and refuses it; no URL library or network fetcher corrects or consumes the target. Keep the byte-escaping feature mapped but unresolved for this reader; do not call it an implementation gap absent a valid reachable case.

The draft has valid one-output controls and records current truncation and Boolean-conversion results. Public Function::eval returns Vec<f32> only, with no runtime error channel; these observations document the architectural limit without asserting parse-time rejection. No Cargo run was made.

requirement: Percent outside a string, and within a content stream, starts a comment extending through bytes before but not including EOL. evidence: skip_whitespace consumes from % up to CR or LF, leaves the marker for the whitespace branch, then continues at the following token. This makes the comment itself separate adjacent regular tokens even without a space before %. The pre-existing lexer assertion `1 % comment\n2` only shows whitespace-plus-comment and LF; the new fixture removes the space before %, includes percent and delimiter-looking bytes inside the comment, and checks CR, LF, and CR-LF endings independently. Type 4 comments have a separate reader in function.rs and its test asserts the comment ends at line boundary. Version headers and %%EOF are separately consumed by §7.5 paths; ordinary comment contents are ignored and not preserved by the writer.

requirement: A supported action in a /Next chain executes at its position in the depth-first sequence, including when a JavaScript action is interleaved with an action performed by the viewer.
source_location: Effective EC3 §12.6.2 Table 196 /Next and Note 1. Table 201 §12.6.4.17 identifies JavaScript as an action type; it remains an action in this common action sequence when the reader has a runner.
errata: No direct erratum to Table 196 /Next or Note 1 found.
evidence: The standard requires the next action after its parent and recursively orders array branches. The action reader flattens supported actions depth-first, and the view-state script walker independently extracts JavaScript in depth-first order. On a public link activation, however, interact::activate first runs every script in the annotation's /A chain, then removes JavaScript refusals from the action vector, then performs the remaining actions in their flattened order. Thus script and non-script actions are not interleaved at their /Next positions. The draft uses a SetOCGState root followed by a JavaScript /Next action and observes the current layer state through ScriptEvent.document; Table 196 order requires the runner to see the layer already ON. A reverse-order positive control (JavaScript root then SetOCGState) requires the runner to see it OFF, while final Query::Layers confirms the later action takes effect. This is public-viewer state observation, not an external test log. Root execution confirms preceding SetOCGState is not reflected in the following script snapshot, although final viewer layers are ON. Reverse JS-then-action sees OFF and final ON as required. This is a selected Link consumer finding; other consumers remain code-supported only.
test_result: FAIL expected in interpolation-mixed-action-target.log, reverse-order and final-state controls PASS
parent_review: Root read Table196/Note1, ADR1602/1750/1752/1904 and actual interact::activate sequence. Corrected ScriptRunners import before compilation. Public-runner snapshot compares cross-kind order with reversed-chain positive control.
